A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CDVAE research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. Content can be matched across relocation and renumbering. The incomplete Causal CPC cells in v2 are visible document content, not extraction failures.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic and semi-synthetic MIMIC-III experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations, sensitivity analyses, and posterior predictive checks.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds hidden-confounding experiments, autoregressive-order diagnostics, representation analysis, and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The CDVAE components, objectives, and Algorithms 1–3 are retained. The encoder description changes from LSTM to GRU, matching the GRU inference network already documented in v2 Appendix G, Table 16; this establishes a documentation correction rather than an architecture change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain synthetic autoregressive data and semi-synthetic MIMIC-III one-step treatment-effect tasks. v3 extends evaluation to hidden-confounding scenarios in both datasets, including withholding four MIMIC-III confounders, without adding a new application domain.

E2.justification: RMSN, CRN, G-Net, Causal Transformer, and Causal CPC remain the evaluated comparators, with the original base/substitute/oracle configurations retained. New comparative analyses reuse these methods. G-Transformer is added only to related work.

E3.justification: v3 introduces several evaluation protocols: training with true autoregressive order 10 and testing masked orders 4–16, controlled hidden-confounding sweeps over Γ=1–5, mutual-information evaluation against latent cluster labels, and scalability sweeps over T=75–175 and covariate dimension 100–500. Original benchmark splits and hyperparameter grids remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 retains the existing component ablations, mixture-component sensitivity, variance trajectories, and posterior predictive checks. It adds finite-memory diagnostics, hidden-confounding robustness tests on both datasets, analysis of latent population-structure recovery, and computational scalability comparisons in Section 6 and Appendices C.3/E.2.

E5.justification: v3 Tables 5–6 introduce Ljung–Box residual-autocorrelation tests, statistics, p-values, and a 0.05 rejection threshold. Ten-seed mean/standard-deviation reporting and posterior predictive p-values already appear in v2; their continued use does not establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial robustness, mutual-information, lag-window, and runtime results. It also revises synthetic Causal CPC values: at heterogeneity coefficient 2.5, base PEHE changes from 7.39±0.29 in v2 Table 4 to 19.39±0.59 in v3 Table 7, aligning with the retained Figure 3, and missing CPC cells are filled. Original CDVAE benchmark scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix E.2 adds Proposition 19, stating per-epoch computational and activation-memory bounds with dependence on sequence length, covariate dimension, and batch size. The existing causal assumptions, identifiability and generalization results, and Appendix A proofs are substantively retained.

C1.justification: The principal contributions remain latent adjustment-variable recovery, ACATE identifiability, near-deterministic consistency, and improved baseline estimates approaching oracle performance. Although v3 replaces ITE wording with CATE/ACATE, v2 already explicitly defined its intended ITE target as ACATE; the underlying estimand and contribution scope are retained.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations connecting recurrent-model memory to CMM assumptions and latent-cluster information to outcome-history proxies. It also adds computational tradeoffs and explicit failure modes covering hidden confounding, time-varying latent variables, infinite-order dependence, heavy-tailed outcomes, and parameter changes. These materially expand the applicability and limitations discussion.

D1.justification: v3 adds an implementation link, NVIDIA Tesla T4 hardware disclosure, training-time information, and hidden-confounding simulation details in Appendix C.1.2. It also reconciles the encoder description with the existing GRU architecture. Most architecture, optimization, and hyperparameter documentation was already present.

R1.justification: v3 adds G-Transformer and references supporting practical adjustment-variable examples, fading-memory arguments, and hidden-confounding sensitivity, including Rosenbaum and Rubin (1983). The central positioning relative to deconfounding and weighted representation learning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 refines treatment-effect terminology, rewrites parts of the abstract and motivation, adds explanatory examples and appendix subsections, and updates publication/contact information. Most existing prose and the overall section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds three comparative figures and six diagnostic, scalability, and timing tables. It reformats ablation Tables 2–3, enlarges and vertically stacks the posterior predictive plots formerly in Figure 7, and improves grouping of the architecture appendix. These substantially expand and revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important gaps in v2 through assumption diagnostics, hidden-confounding tests, population-structure analysis, explicit failure conditions, and runtime measurements. Completing and correcting the Causal CPC table also resolves incomplete and contradictory reporting. Some new scalability prose is imprecise—Table 10 shows nearly constant runtime as covariate dimension grows—but the gains in empirical scrutiny, transparency, and practical guidance are substantial.
